INDEPENDENT MIXED BULK/TRACE ENERGY THEOREM
Frozen-phase proof candidate; final checkpoint scope only.
Agent: complexity_proof_recon, 2026-10-09.

0. Scope, exposure, and proof status

This packet answers the mixed quadratic energy question assigned by root.
It does not claim any geometric recovery, varifold transfer, rectifiability,
or downstream application. No current nonlinear/recovery report was read.
The proof below was independently reconstructed using dyadic frequency and
physical scales. Root's subsequent hyperplane/carre-du-champ calibration
message supplied motivation, not a proof premise. No advanced trace theorem,
measure regularity theorem, or unpublished sibling proof is assumed.

The argument uses Fourier inversion and Plancherel for Schwartz functions,
Cauchy-Schwarz, Tonelli/Fatou, elementary ball covering, and the elementary
sequence convolution inequality, whose needed instance is proved below.
All measure-specific and mixed-energy estimates are derived here. No primary
literature search was technically needed; no historical or novelty assertion
is made. At original freeze this is a complete analytic internal candidate,
fresh independent review pending; external/formal validation and priority are
UNKNOWN. Preservation hashes are evidence of provenance, not proof validity.

1. Exact global theorem

Let m >= 2. There is a constant C_m, depending only on m, with the following
property. Let sigma be a nonnegative Radon measure on R^m and A >= 0, and assume

  sigma(B_r(x)) <= A r^(m-1)             for every x in R^m and every r > 0. (1.1)

For every real or complex u in C_c^infinity(R^m), define the extended positive
integral

  J_sigma(u) = int_Rm sigma(dx) int_Rm
                 |u(y)-u(x)|^2 / |x-y|^(m+1) dy.                          (1.2)

The value assigned on x=y is irrelevant: for each x the Lebesgue y-measure of
that point is zero. Then

  J_sigma(u) <= C_m A int_Rm |grad u|^2 dy.                                (1.3)

In particular the integral is finite. Finiteness of sigma is not needed;
finite sigma, as in the assigned question, is included. There is no lower
density, doubling, rectifiability, uniform rectifiability, or supporting-plane
assumption. No extra L^2 term is needed under the global hypothesis (1.1).

We prove the following slightly more general estimate, in the same argument:
if A_1,A_0 >= 0 and

  sigma(B_r(x)) <= A_1

INDEPENDENT THEOREM-FIRST MIXED-TRACE BASELINE

Outcome: a COMPLETE analytic proof of the exact proposed inequality is
obtained by a frequency decomposition. Candidate files were not opened.
Status is internally reconstructed, not externally/formally verified or
a novelty claim. No rectifiability or lower-density assumption is used.
All previous packets are immutable; this task has no application extension.

1. EXACT STATEMENT AND CONVENTIONS

For m>=2, let sigma be a nonnegative Radon measure on R^m satisfying
  sigma(B_r(x))<=A r^(m-1) for EVERY x in R^m and EVERY r>0.  (1.1)
Let u in C_c^infinity(R^m) be scalar, real or complex. Then
  J(u)=integral sigma(dx) integral dy
           |u(y)-u(x)|^2/|x-y|^(m+1)
       <=C_m A integral |grad u|^2 dy,                      (1.2)
with a finite constant depending only on m. Infinite total sigma mass is
allowed. Every value at a sigma point is the actual smooth function value;
no representative of a Lebesgue-a.e. Sobolev class is substituted.
If A=0, sigma=0 and the conclusion is immediate. Below assume A>0.

Changing variables y=x+h rewrites the nonnegative extended integral as
  J(u)=integral dh/|h|^(m+1) ||u(.+h)-u||_(L^2(sigma))^2.  (1.3)
We will prove finiteness rather than assume it. Only ordinary Fourier
inversion, Plancherel, weighted Cauchy, Tonelli/Fatou, and summable sequence
convolution are used; the needed band trace estimate is proved here.

2. GROWTH ALONE GIVES THE BANDLIMITED TRACE ESTIMATE

Let g be a Schwartz function with Fourier support in |xi|<=2lambda.
Fix a smooth compactly supported Fourier cutoff eta equal to 1 on B2,
and let K be its inverse Fourier transform. Set K_lambda(x)=lambda^m K(lambda x).
Then g=K_lambda*g POINTWISE, and ||K_lambda||_1=||K||_1. Weighted Cauchy
gives
  |g(x)|^2<=||K||_1 integral |K_lambda(x-z)||g(z)|^2 dz.
For any fixed M>m-1, the Schwartz estimate and growth (1.1), summed over
the ball of radius lambda^-1 and the doubling annuli, give
  sup_z integral |K_lambda(x-z)| sigma(dx)
    <=C_m A lambda^m lambda^(-(m-1))
         [1+sum_{ell>=0}2^(-ell M)2^((ell+1)(m-1))]
    <=C_m A lambda.
All cutoffs and M can be fixed once for each dimension. Tonelli therefore
proves
  ||g||_(L^2(sigma))^2<=C_m A lambda ||g||_(L^2(dy))^2.     (2.1)
Every translate of sigma satisfies (1.1) with the SAME A. Thus (2.1)
also holds for g(.+v), uniformly in v. No geometric fact about sigma
